observations.why: The adoption statement performs a decision on behalf of the organization, with no explicit reciprocal or pooled-relations cue.
The quantified performance comparison frames the choice through proportional benefit.
The asserted schedule carries an organizational allocation of action and timing, but no explicit rank or command form.
The labeled summary presents the database choice as a settled organizational decision.
The labeled metric frames the choice through proportional performance gain.
The labeled timeline presents organizational action as assigned and fixed, without explicit command or deference.
